acceptanceCriteria: A healthy binding lists key metadata and fingerprints through redacted DTOs without returning key values
The management credential is resolved only inside the adapter and a completion-endpoint probe rejects it
Code, config, process-wide environment, model context, job payloads, logs, errors, API responses, and receipts contain no management key
Cross-workspace, stale-generation, wrong-account, and unapproved management operations fail before a provider call
Disabling the binding prevents new rotations and leaves existing runtime keys unchanged pending explicit reconciliation
userStories.description: Implement an OpenRouter AuthorityProviderAdapter using a core ProviderBinding and SecretStore reference for the management key. Expose semantic list, create-limited-key, disable, delete, and verify operations; never return the management credential. Store provider account identity, binding generation, policy limits, fingerprints, and resource ids in core records; add no provider-specific secret column or child migration. Preflight verifies the management endpoint, account binding, scope, and the documented invariant that the management credential cannot call completion endpoints.
userStories.title: OpenRouter management bindings expose lifecycle operations but never inference

acceptanceCriteria: Changing the provider binding, current fingerprint, limits, target binding, canary, timeout, or rollback action changes the digest and invalidates approval
Concurrent and replayed execution creates at most one replacement key for the rotation intent
Crash after provider acceptance reconciles the replacement by stable metadata and records its provider resource id before continuing
Every created key is tracked as pending, active, revoked, cleanup-required, or reconciled; unknown is not a terminal state
A replacement key receives only the declared limits and cannot be used across another workspace or environment binding
userStories.description: Define an immutable rotation intent containing provider binding, current runtime-key fingerprint/reference, desired name, credit and usage limits, target RuntimeSecretBindingAdapter reference, canary contract, timeout, rollback action, and exact request digest. Create a distinctly named limited replacement under the core idempotency/fencing state machine. If outcome is uncertain, list provider keys by stable intent metadata before creating another. Parent and replacement secret values stay inside SecretStore and trusted adapters.
userStories.title: One rotation intent creates at most one bounded replacement key

acceptanceCriteria: The old key remains active while the replacement binding, target revision, and real provider-backed completion canary are pending
A health-only response cannot satisfy the canary contract
Canary success records the target binding generation and deployed revision before disabling the old key
Cutover disables the old key, verifies old-key rejection, settles the new key active, and emits one redacted receipt
An unavailable target-binding adapter produces durable WAITING_FOR_AUTHORIZATION without consuming story execution timeout
userStories.description: Stage the replacement through the generic RuntimeSecretBindingAdapter, deploy or refresh the target when the binding requires it, and run the declared real OpenRouter completion through that target surface rather than a health-only endpoint. Keep the old key active until the target revision and completion result pass. Then atomically mark the new binding active, disable the old provider key, and verify old-key rejection. Do not depend on Coolify specifically; a Coolify implementation may satisfy the binding contract later.
userStories.title: Canary success cuts over the target before the old key is revoked

acceptanceCriteria: Every failed pre-cutover path leaves the prior key active and the target functional
A changed target binding is restored to its prior generation before the failed replacement is disabled or deleted
Crash at each external boundary resumes or reconciles once without duplicate keys or untracked target bindings
An uncertain old-key disable is read back before any retry and cannot disable the replacement by mistake
No failure log, exception, receipt, WAL event, or API response contains either key value
userStories.description: Implement rollback for provider creation failure, target-binding failure, deploy failure, canary failure, cutover uncertainty, old-key disable failure, and receipt/revocation failure. Restore the prior target binding when changed, retain the old key when safe, disable/delete the failed replacement, and emit a rollback or reconciliation-required receipt. Inject crashes after key creation, binding stage, deploy acceptance, canary result, cutover, and old-key disable.
userStories.title: Failure restores the prior target and reconciles every created key

acceptanceCriteria: The bounded live fixture records successful replacement, real inference, cutover, old-key rejection, and provider resource cleanup within the declared spend limit
Prompt extraction, cross-workspace/environment use, altered intent, replay, expired grant, and revoked-key reuse all fail
Injected crashes leave the target functional and every provider key in a known reconciled state
The adapter remains unavailable without an explicit healthy binding and accepted rotation policy
Qualification and rollback require no Categoric/Cashflow-App code, environment, credential, or workspace
userStories.description: Qualify against a dedicated low-limit OpenRouter test account/binding and a disposable Rorca-owned target-binding fixture. Exercise real management API lifecycle, real inference canary, cutover, old-key rejection, rollback, replay, cross-scope denial, prompt extraction attempts, and crash recovery. Keep rollout off by default; enable per verified workspace binding only. Rollback disables the adapter, restores the prior binding where possible, revokes replacements, and preserves receipts. Non-goals are alternate LLM providers, customer environment changes, billing management, and automated production rotation without explicit policy.
userStories.title: A bounded live rotation proves security before workspace rollout
